page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring dedicated AMD EPYC processor hardware on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading active at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside vector instruction support such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a compute-aligned ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements reflect robust multi-threaded CPU throughput. The instance ranks in the top 10 percent of servers in stress-ng single-core performance with a score of 3,144.37, alongside a strong stress-ng multi-core result of 100,519.25. Geekbench testing yields a multi-core score of 16,041.0, marked by high throughput in software compilation with Clang (41,690.0) and ray tracing (50,430.0). PassMark benchmarks confirm strong compute execution with a CPU score of 51,157.15 and encryption score of 39,771.17. For small-scale language model inference, text generation on a 135M parameter model achieves top-tier throughput of 339.19 tokens per second.

Memory bandwidth and storage-adjacent transactional operations remain in the mid-range tier, exhibiting 124.41 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth, 67.54 GB/sec write bandwidth, and 46.76 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Static web serving throughput reaches 25.94 GB/sec. The instance delivers favorable compute density by allocating dedicated hardware cores and fast local NVMe storage, though applications requiring extensive memory-to-core ratios or massive sequential memory bandwidth will find memory capacity constrained relative to the high core count.

The hardware configuration is well matched for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Key target applications include CI/CD build environments, software compilation, medium-scale mathematical simulations, batch cryptography processing, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is a compute-focused instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores at 2.0 GHz. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the platform includes AVX-512 instruction extensions, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks place its raw multi-core compute in the upper quartile, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 51,157.15 and strong software compilation throughput. Memory bandwidth and transactional operations operate within average performance boundaries. With a 2 GB per vCPU allocation, the instance trades high per-core memory capacity for concentrated processing power. It is suitable for continuous integration, code compilation pipelines, cryptographic batch workloads, and CPU-driven inference tasks.
